gap.description: Almost every result is generic gym-blog content written to rank, not from someone who actually teaches self-defense-relevant sparring day to day. Only 1 of 5 (Lotus Fitness) shows real E-E-A-T with a named coach and honest limitations; none show real training footage, real student outcomes, or the Thailand-specific angle of training where Muay Thai actually comes from (vs. a Western commercial gym teaching a diluted version). No result addresses how a family-friendly, beginner-first camp abroad approaches self-defense differently than a hardcore competition gym.

weakness: no result cites any data, study, or real incident/statistic about self-defense effectiveness
most results avoid honestly naming Muay Thai's real limitation (no ground game) except Lotus Fitness
no result speaks to complete beginners or families/travelers wondering if short-term training abroad is 'enough' for self-defense
CTAs are all local-gym-directory style, disconnected from the actual topic (no global or travel-training angle)
recommended_angle: Write an honest, coach-voiced answer (not brand copy): yes, Muay Thai builds real self-defense tools (clinch, knees, elbows, checking kicks, distance management) but it is not a magic bullet — no ground game, and awareness/avoidance still matter more than any strike. Differentiate with Wildcat's warm, family-first framing: what a few weeks of training at an authentic Chiang Mai camp realistically gives a beginner (confidence + a handful of reliable, low-setup techniques), paired with real coach perspective from Meaw's team rather than generic gym-blog claims — avoiding 'warrior' hype entirely.
